hero.headline: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement funding through 2028
hero.body:
The Senate voted early Friday morning to fund President Trump's immigration enforcement agencies through the end of his second term, allocating $70 billion to Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol operations over the next three years.

The legislation passed on a party-line vote of 52-47 following an 18-hour marathon session known as a "vote-a-rama," during which senators proposed unlimited amendments. Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska was the only member of her party to vote against the bill, while Democratic Senator Michael Bennet of Colorado did not vote.

The passage came after weeks of uncertainty and fierce internal debate over controversial provisions. A central point of contention was a proposed $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund that would allow the administration to issue financial settlements to people connected to the January 6 insurrection. Senate Democrats attempted to strip this provision from the bill through an amendment introduced by Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer. The amendment failed by a single vote, 49-50, with three vulnerable Republican senators breaking ranks to join all Democrats in support.

The debate also involved Republican resistance to initially proposed spending for White House renovations, which Senate leadership ultimately dropped from the bill.

Democratic Senator Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota expressed her frustration with the outcome. "Your tax dollars should not be going to Jan. 6th rioters who went after officers," she wrote on X. "And why give MORE money to ICE when they're already bigger than the FBI?"

Democratic Senator Alex Padilla of California highlighted concerns about immigration enforcement practices, citing deaths of Americans and detention of children, stating that thousands of children have been jailed since the administration began and that ICE has been found to violate the Constitution in more than 10,000 rulings by judges appointed by both Democratic and Republican presidents.

Republican supporters characterized the funding as essential. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Republicans were prioritizing Trump's interests over working families. "The Republican agenda is now written in black and white: A slush fund for Trump, tax dodges for Trump, a ballroom for Trump, and a private militia for Trump. For hard-working Americans? Nothing," Schumer stated.

In contrast, Republican Senator Lindsey Graham expressed satisfaction with the outcome, saying he was "very proud of my Republican colleagues for sticking together and making sure that Border Patrol and ICE are fully funded."

The bill now moves to the House of Representatives for consideration, where it is expected to be taken up next week. The legislation represents a major priority for the Trump administration, securing resources for immigration enforcement operations throughout the remainder of his term.

cards.headline: US-Brokered Lebanon Cease-Fire Stalls as Hezbollah Rejects Terms
cards.body:
A United States-led cease-fire agreement between Israel and Lebanon has failed to stop fighting, with Hezbollah continuing attacks despite the deal reached on April 17. The Iranian-backed group has rejected the terms, stating they do not consider themselves bound by negotiations conducted without their participation.

Since the cease-fire began, Hezbollah has launched drone attacks against Israeli soldiers in south Lebanon on a nearly daily basis. On Tuesday, the group conducted several drone strikes using fiber-optic-guided aircraft that have evaded Israeli air defenses. An Israeli soldier was killed and six others wounded in a Hezbollah drone attack on Sunday. The armed group claims its Tuesday attacks injured additional Israeli soldiers, though the Israeli military has not confirmed casualties beyond reporting that it fired interceptor missiles.

Israel has responded with continued airstrikes and new displacement orders. On Tuesday alone, Israeli forces ordered residents of 16 villages in south Lebanon to evacuate northward. Over the weekend, Israeli airstrikes killed 18 people and wounded 88 more in Lebanon, according to the Lebanese health ministry. Since fighting began on March 2, at least 2,534 people have been killed and 7,863 wounded by Israeli airstrikes in Lebanon.

The cease-fire agreement permits Israel to conduct strikes in self-defense, language identical to a previous 2024 cease-fire during which Israel struck Lebanon more than 15,000 times. Israel has established a "yellow line" in south Lebanon comprising at least 55 villages, where Israeli troops remain active and have continued demolishing homes.

Hezbollah leadership has explicitly rejected the agreement. Naim Qassem, the group's head, called direct negotiations between the Lebanese government and Israel a "grave sin" that would plunge the country into instability. He stated that the group will not disarm, a key Israeli demand. The Lebanese government responded that "real betrayal" comes from those who drag their country into war for foreign interests.

The collapse of cease-fire enforcement reflects the limited authority of the Lebanese government over Hezbollah. While Lebanese officials negotiate in Washington, they cannot control the armed group's military operations. This dynamic has prompted US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to suggest the United States could help Lebanon develop specialized army units to confront Hezbollah directly, a prospect that has alarmed Lebanese officials concerned about sparking civil conflict.

Israeli officials continue applying pressure, with Defense Minister Israel Katz accusing the Lebanese government of taking cover under Hezbollah rather than acting forcefully against the group. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Hezbollah retains about 10 percent of its original missiles and promised continued strikes on what he termed Hezbollah infrastructure both inside and north of the security zone.

The United States asked Israel to ensure any response to Hezbollah attacks remained "calculated and limited."

cards.headline: Senate Democrats block surveillance law extension over intelligence director appointment
cards.teaser: Democrats prevented debate from starting on extending spy powers due to expire next week.
cards.body:
Senate Democrats blocked a procedural motion early Friday to begin debate on extending enhanced surveillance authorities set to expire June 12. All Senate Democrats except John Fetterman of Pennsylvania voted against the motion.

The blockade protests President Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence. The Section 702 foreign surveillance authority, which enables expanded monitoring of foreign targets, faces lapse without congressional action.

cards.headline: Jobs Report Shows Recovery After Stagnant 2025
cards.teaser: Economic data indicate a labor market rebound, though workforce growth constraints may limit overall expansion.
cards.body:
The latest jobs report showed signs of economic recovery following a stagnant 2025. Data released Friday pointed to improvement in employment conditions compared to the previous year's sluggish performance.

Analysts noted that slow workforce growth could limit the pace of broader economic expansion despite the positive employment trends. The report provided evidence that labor market conditions have stabilized after last year's difficulties.

cards.headline: Italy Calls for New European Military Alliance Independent of US
cards.teaser: Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto said European nations should create their own joint defense system and assume greater responsibility for their security.
cards.body:
Italy's defense minister Guido Crosetto has called for European nations to establish their own joint defense system, arguing that Europe must take greater responsibility for its security. His comments reflect concerns among European leaders about the reliability of American security commitments.

Crosetto's proposal suggests a shift away from the current defense architecture centered on NATO and US involvement. The minister emphasized that Europe needs to develop independent military capabilities and strengthen coordination structures among member states to protect the continent without depending on American support.

cards.headline: Armenian Prime Minister Faces Election Backed by Trump, Opposed by Putin
cards.teaser: Nikol Pashinyan is seeking re-election as Armenia weighs questions of war, peace, and whether to align with Russia or the West.
cards.body:
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is campaigning for re-election in a contest that has drawn international attention. The Trump administration has expressed support for Pashinyan, while Russian President Vladimir Putin has opposed his re-election bid.

The election reflects fundamental choices about Armenia's future direction. Pashinyan's tenure has centered on questions about the country's geopolitical alignment, its relationship with neighboring Azerbaijan, and whether Armenia will move toward Western institutions or maintain its traditional ties with Russia. The election outcome will significantly influence Armenia's foreign policy and security arrangements.

cards.headline: US Journalist Pleads Guilty to Acting as Chinese Agent
cards.teaser: Thomas Weir Pauken II admitted to working with Chinese government employees for years without registering as a foreign agent.
cards.body:
Thomas Weir Pauken II, a 50-year-old American journalist, has pleaded guilty to knowingly working as an agent for the Chinese government. He maintained contact with people employed by Beijing for years without proper registration.

The case underscores concerns about foreign influence operations within American media. Federal law requires those working on behalf of foreign governments to register and disclose such relationships.

cards.headline: Nearly 50 Die of Thirst After Lorry Breaks Down in Sahara Desert
cards.teaser: Only two people survived a journey across the Sahara after their vehicle broke down, forcing them to trek more than 50 kilometers for help.
cards.body:
Nearly 50 people died of thirst in the Sahara desert after their lorry broke down in a remote area. Only two passengers survived the tragedy.

The two survivors trekked more than 50 kilometers across the desert to reach authorities and alert them to the disaster. By the time rescue teams were dispatched and arrived at the scene, the other passengers had already succumbed to dehydration in the extreme desert conditions.

cards.headline: Gold Mining Accelerates Ebola Spread in Remote Congo Town
cards.teaser: Mining activity in a Congolese hill town is fueling the spread of an Ebola outbreak that has devastated the remote community.
cards.body:
Gold mining has become a major factor in spreading Ebola through a remote town in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The mining industry, which has sustained the hillside community for decades, is now enabling the virus to move between workers and their families.

Health officials are struggling to contain the outbreak as miners continue working in close quarters and traveling between sites. The economic necessity of mining work conflicts with public health measures designed to limit contact and movement. The outbreak has proven particularly difficult to control given the remote location and the population's dependence on mining for survival.

cards.headline: France Releases Criminal Record of Child Murder Suspect
cards.teaser: A man suspected of murdering an 11-year-old girl had been previously identified as a potential child molester, according to released records.
cards.body:
French authorities have released criminal records revealing that a man suspected of murdering an 11-year-old girl was previously identified as a potential child molester. The disclosure has triggered widespread public anger over the suspect's handling and monitoring prior to the alleged crime.

The case has intensified debate in France about how individuals flagged as threats to children are supervised. The records release has prompted calls for reforms to child protection systems and criminal monitoring procedures.

hero.headline: Public health officials prepare for World Cup health risks amid Ebola concerns
hero.body:
Public health departments across the United States are developing medical response plans ahead of the World Cup, focusing on common health threats that emerge when large crowds gather while also monitoring disease surveillance efforts.

The preparations underscore how local and state health agencies have taken on expanded responsibility for managing public health during major events. With reduced federal public health infrastructure, these departments are coordinating their own surveillance systems and treatment protocols to address health scenarios that typically arise during international sporting events.

Officials are preparing strategies to handle infectious diseases, heat-related illnesses, and bacterial infections. The planning reflects standard protocols that health departments implement whenever increased population density and travel create conditions for disease transmission.

Disease surveillance represents a key component of the World Cup preparations. Health officials emphasized that their planning is precautionary and designed to address the range of common health issues that typically emerge during large sporting events. The coordination between local health departments ensures that adequate medical resources and rapid response capabilities will be available throughout the tournament.

Public health authorities are also monitoring ongoing disease outbreaks as part of their broader surveillance efforts. While officials have not indicated that specific threats pose a direct risk to World Cup attendees, health departments are maintaining awareness of developing situations that could affect public health during the event.

The shift toward local and state health agencies managing major event health security reflects broader changes in public health infrastructure. These departments are working to ensure they have the systems, personnel, and resources needed to respond quickly if health issues emerge during the tournament.

The World Cup preparations highlight the importance of coordination between different levels of government and health agencies. By establishing protocols and communication systems in advance, health officials aim to minimize response times and ensure effective management of any health concerns that arise.

Public health departments have experience managing health security at large events, and the World Cup preparations follow established frameworks that have been refined through previous international gatherings. Officials are drawing on this experience to anticipate potential challenges and develop appropriate responses.

The focus on common health ailments reflects the reality that heat stress, dehydration, and infectious diseases spread through close contact represent the most likely health challenges during crowded sporting events. By preparing response strategies for these issues, health departments aim to prevent minor health problems from becoming widespread concerns.

Overall, the World Cup health preparations demonstrate how public health agencies at local and state levels are stepping into roles previously handled with greater federal involvement. Through coordinated planning and disease surveillance, these departments are working to ensure that fans can safely gather for the tournament.

cards.headline: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement funding bill
cards.teaser: The Senate approved legislation providing three years of funding for ICE and Border Patrol after an 18-hour voting session.
cards.body:
The Senate passed a $70 billion immigration enforcement bill early Friday morning with a 52-47 vote, following an 18-hour overnight voting session. The legislation funds Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol operations for the next three years through the end of President Trump's term. Democrats had blocked the funding for months before the bill's passage.

The vote came after weeks of delays triggered by controversy over an unrelated $1.776 billion settlement fund. Senators rejected efforts to permanently block Trump from reviving the settlement fund. The bill now advances to the House of Representatives for consideration next week.

cards.headline: SpaceX to allow individual investors to purchase shares
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's aerospace company will open share purchases to individual investors starting next week.
cards.body:
Individual investors will be able to buy shares in SpaceX beginning next week, marking a shift in how the company allows public participation in its equity. The company, owned by Elon Musk, has expanded from rocket manufacturing into artificial intelligence ventures.

SpaceX has historically limited share ownership, but the new policy will permit retail investors to take stakes in the company. The move represents a significant change in accessibility for individuals seeking investment opportunities in private aerospace and technology ventures.

cards.headline: Paddleboard company owner's sentence appeal denied after four deaths
cards.teaser: Nerys Lloyd, serving over 10 years for gross negligence manslaughter, had her request to reduce her sentence rejected.
cards.body:
A paddleboard firm owner has failed in her bid to reduce her sentence for gross negligence manslaughter. Nerys Lloyd was handed a 10-year and six-month prison term in April 2025 after being convicted of causing four deaths through her business operations.

The court's refusal to cut her sentence means Lloyd will continue serving the full term originally imposed for the convictions.

cards.headline: Former student charged after crossbow attack at University of Surrey
cards.teaser: A campus safety officer suffered serious injuries in an attack at the Guildford university on Thursday.
cards.body:
Police charged a former student following a crossbow attack at the University of Surrey campus in Guildford. The incident occurred on Thursday and left a university campus safety officer with serious injuries.

The attack took place on the university grounds, prompting a police response and investigation. Authorities have taken the former student into custody on charges related to the assault on the security officer.

cards.headline: UK military chief warns of heightened security threats from Russia
cards.teaser: Chief of Defence Staff Sir Richard Knighton said Russian activities targeting UK defenses represent the most dangerous period he has witnessed.
cards.body:
Britain's military leader has described the current security environment as the most dangerous he has experienced in his career. Chief of the Defence Staff Sir Richard Knighton told the BBC that Russian incursions into UK defences pose a significant risk.

Knighton warned that Russian activities threaten to cross a critical threshold, reflecting escalating concerns about hostile military and intelligence operations targeting British security infrastructure.

cards.headline: Court documents reveal Andrew sub-let Royal Lodge cottages
cards.teaser: A public spending watchdog disclosed that Prince Andrew had been renting out properties on the Royal Lodge estate.
cards.body:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor sub-let cottages at Royal Lodge, according to documents released by a public spending watchdog. The disclosure came as part of an examination of property arrangements involving members of the royal family.

The watchdog's review included scrutiny of how royals manage properties under their control. The revelation about the cottage rentals at Royal Lodge adds detail to ongoing questions about royal property use and financial arrangements.

hero.headline: SpaceX Opens to Individual Investors Starting Next Week
hero.body:
SpaceX is preparing for the largest initial public offering in US stock market history, with plans to debut on June 12 and raise up to $75 billion. The company released a detailed investor prospectus this week, marking a significant shift for Elon Musk's private space and artificial intelligence company, which has previously limited ownership to institutional investors and employees.

The offering values SpaceX at $1.77 trillion, potentially positioning founder Musk to become the world's first trillionaire. The prospectus reveals financial details about SpaceX's operations and future ambitions while also disclosing numerous quirks and risks associated with the company and its interconnected businesses.

SpaceX's filings show extensive financial ties to other Musk enterprises. The company spent $506 million purchasing Tesla's Megapack battery products in 2025 and $191 million in 2024. More notably, SpaceX acquired $131 million worth of Cybertrucks at manufacturer's suggested retail prices last year, purchasing at least 1,300 vehicles. This represented a significant portion of Tesla's total Cybertruck sales of 20,237 units for the year.

The prospectus emphasizes SpaceX's broader mission beyond commercial spaceflight. The company frames its ultimate goal as establishing permanent colonies on the moon and Mars to ensure human survival and "extend the light of consciousness to the stars." Musk is eligible to receive an award of 1 billion shares if SpaceX achieves the establishment of a permanent human colony on Mars with at least 1 million inhabitants.

The filings also outline substantial risks to investors. SpaceX acquired the artificial intelligence company xAI in February, and the prospectus warns about risks posed by xAI's Grok chatbot. The document discloses that Grok's "spicy" and "unhinged" modes present heightened risks of generating explicit content, misinformation, nonconsensual imagery, and other harmful outputs. The Center for Countering Digital Hate estimated that Grok generated more than 3 million sexualized images in just 11 days earlier this year before the company increased restrictions.

SpaceX's financial filings reveal other notable expenses. The company spent $4 million in 2025 on Musk's personal security through his private security firm, with spending increasing from $2 million in 2023 and $3 million in 2024.

The prospectus also highlights significant financial challenges. SpaceX reported losses of $4.9 billion as a result of its massive spending, and the company discloses that it may never become profitable, presenting a substantial risk to investors despite its market-leading position in commercial spaceflight and satellite operations.

The IPO represents an unprecedented opportunity for retail investors to own shares in a company controlling critical infrastructure for both commercial and government space operations.

cards.headline: Jobs Report Shows Recovery After Stagnant 2025
cards.teaser: Economic data indicate a labor market rebound, though workforce growth constraints may limit overall expansion.
cards.body:
The latest jobs report showed signs of economic recovery following a stagnant 2025. Data released Friday pointed to improvement in employment conditions compared to the previous year's sluggish performance.

Analysts noted that slow workforce growth could limit the pace of broader economic expansion despite the positive employment trends. The report provided evidence that labor market conditions have stabilized after last year's difficulties.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Falls Near $62,000 in Week of Crypto Losses
cards.teaser: Bitcoin hit its longest losing streak since August as cryptocurrency markets declined sharply.
cards.body:
Bitcoin dropped to near $62,000 on Friday, capping a difficult week for cryptocurrency markets. The decline marked Bitcoin's longest losing streak since August and left the digital currency trading roughly 50 percent below its all-time high.

The selloff extended beyond Bitcoin, with ether and privacy-focused cryptocurrencies also posting significant losses. The HYPE token fell 14 percent as investors moved away from AI-related crypto assets. Market analysts tied the broader crypto decline to an unwinding of trades linked to artificial intelligence investments.

cards.headline: New Graduates Face Weak Job Market With Long-Term Wage Effects
cards.teaser: Recent college graduates are struggling to find work in a hiring downturn that economists say could affect earnings for years.
cards.body:
Recent college graduates are struggling to secure jobs in today's weak hiring market. According to labor economists, entering the workforce during economic downturns can have long-lasting consequences for earnings and career growth.

Historical evidence shows that workers who start their careers during recessions or sluggish hiring periods typically earn significantly less than graduates from stronger economic periods, with wage gaps often persisting for more than a decade. The full extent of this downturn's impact on current graduates remains to be seen, particularly regarding how artificial intelligence will affect entry-level positions and career development.

cards.headline: Mattel Bets on He-Man Franchise as Entertainment Strategy
cards.teaser: The toy maker is testing whether Masters of the Universe can establish the company as an entertainment powerhouse.
cards.body:
Mattel is pursuing an entertainment strategy built around Masters of the Universe, the 1980s franchise centered on the He-Man character. The company is testing whether the hypermasculine character can serve as the foundation for a broader entertainment empire.

The move represents Mattel's effort to position itself as more than a toy manufacturer. The company has been working to develop its intellectual property into films, television shows, and other media content, following strategies used by competitors to extend brand value beyond physical products.

cards.headline: Anthropic Co-Founder Warns Against Autonomous AI Development
cards.teaser: Jack Clark said artificial intelligence could reach a point where it develops without human input.
cards.body:
Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said the artificial intelligence industry needs to prevent AI systems from developing without human oversight. Clark told BBC's Newsnight that AI technology could advance to a stage where it evolves independently of human guidance.

The warning comes as major AI companies race to develop increasingly capable systems. Clark's comments reflect growing concern within parts of the AI research community about maintaining human control over advanced artificial intelligence development.

cards.headline: Ram Releases Fuel-Intensive Muscle Trucks With Patriotic Marketing
cards.teaser: The automaker is betting that American men will buy high-performance trucks despite elevated gas prices.
cards.body:
Ram introduced a new line of fuel-intensive muscle trucks aimed at American buyers, particularly men. The company launched advertising featuring cowboys and American flags to promote the vehicles despite current gas prices.

Automakers continue to prioritize truck sales in the American market, where pickup trucks remain popular. The new Ram models emphasize performance over fuel efficiency, a strategy that reflects manufacturer confidence in sustained demand for large, powerful vehicles regardless of fuel costs.

hero.headline: Valve confirms Steam Machine gaming console will ship this summer
hero.body:
Valve has announced that its Steam Machine console and Steam Frame VR headset will launch this summer, according to a blog post from the company detailing its hardware verification programs.

The Steam Machine represents Valve's effort to bring its PC gaming library into living rooms through a dedicated console device. By releasing both the Steam Machine and Steam Frame alongside verification programs for developers, Valve is signaling that both products have progressed far enough in development to warrant a public launch timeline.

The verification programs mentioned in Valve's announcement suggest the company is preparing its ecosystem to support these new hardware platforms. These programs typically help ensure games run smoothly on specific devices and provide developers with guidelines for optimization.

Valve has been working on expanding its hardware offerings beyond the Steam Deck handheld system. The company's hardware strategy has evolved significantly over the past several years, beginning with the Steam Controller and continuing through the successful launch of the Steam Deck portable gaming device. The Steam Machine and Steam Frame represent the next phase of this expansion into different form factors.

The summer launch window places both devices in direct competition with established players in the console market. Sony's PlayStation, Microsoft's Xbox, and Nintendo's Switch currently dominate the home gaming space. Valve's approach leverages its existing Steam platform, which contains tens of thousands of games and millions of active users worldwide.

Valve has traditionally taken a cautious approach to hardware releases, conducting extensive internal testing and refinement before launching products. The company has previously delayed hardware when it failed to meet internal quality standards. The confirmation of a summer release timeline suggests both the Steam Machine and Steam Frame have reached production readiness.

Details about the Steam Frame remain limited beyond its confirmed summer launch window. Valve has not yet provided extensive specifications or feature details about either device through the channels reported.

The announcement comes as Valve continues to invest heavily in its broader ecosystem. The company has built a reputation for supporting its hardware products with regular software updates and ongoing community engagement. This track record may influence how developers and consumers respond to the new hardware announcements.

The Steam Machine's entry into the console market will likely depend heavily on how well Valve can demonstrate the advantages of its ecosystem compared to competitors. The existing Steam library and user base represent significant advantages, but the company will need to convince consumers that the Steam Machine offers compelling reasons to choose it over more established alternatives in the crowded home console market.

cards.headline: Microsoft AI chief says Anthropic models are too expensive
cards.teaser: Microsoft's artificial intelligence chief stated that Anthropic's AI models carry too high a cost for the company's needs.
cards.body:
Microsoft's AI leadership has raised concerns about the cost of Anthropic's models as companies assess pricing from different large language model providers. The comments reflect Microsoft's broader AI strategy, which centers on its significant investments in OpenAI and the integration of AI capabilities across its product ecosystem, including Windows and Azure cloud services.

At its Build 2026 developer conference, Microsoft announced Project Solara, an Android-based operating system designed specifically for AI agents. The company also introduced new tools for developing agent-driven applications through Microsoft Fabric and Microsoft Databases, signaling its focus on agent-based AI rather than traditional software applications.

cards.headline: Anthropic revenue reaches $47 billion ahead of planned IPO
cards.teaser: Anthropic announced its annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May as the company prepares for a public stock offering.
cards.body:
Anthropic's annualized revenue surpassed $47 billion in May, representing explosive growth from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025. The company has achieved this trajectory while competing against OpenAI, Google, and other major AI players in an increasingly crowded market.

As Anthropic moves toward its initial public offering, President Daniela Amodei has addressed investor concerns about the long-term returns on AI investments. The company's steep revenue growth will face scrutiny from potential investors evaluating the profitability prospects of large language model businesses.

cards.headline: Paleontologists discover four-winged velociraptor cousin in China
cards.teaser: Researchers identified a new dinosaur species related to velociraptors that likely glided on four wings and hunted early birds from trees.
cards.body:
Paleontologists have identified a new dinosaur species in China that represents a relative of the velociraptor. The creature featured four wings and is believed to have been a gliding predator, similar to how modern flying squirrels move through trees.

The fossil suggests this dinosaur hunted birds while positioned in the canopy of ancient Chinese forests. Its four-winged structure would have enabled it to navigate through the treetops while pursuing prey, providing new insights into how certain dinosaur lineages evolved flight-related adaptations.

cards.headline: Geomagnetic storm may produce northern lights across northern US states
cards.teaser: A powerful geomagnetic storm could make the aurora borealis visible as far south as Illinois and Oregon.
cards.body:
Space weather forecasters issued a G3-class geomagnetic storm watch for June 4-5. Four coronal mass ejections from the sun are heading toward Earth, creating conditions that could produce visible auroras at lower latitudes than usual. States including Utah, North Carolina, Vermont, New York, and New Hampshire may see displays.

The storm results from solar activity that launched charged particles toward Earth. When these particles interact with the planet's magnetic field and atmosphere, they create the colorful light displays known as auroras. The phenomenon typically occurs near the poles but becomes visible farther south during stronger geomagnetic events.

cards.headline: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky plans to launch new AI research lab
cards.teaser: Airbnb chief executive Brian Chesky announced plans to establish an artificial intelligence laboratory focused on the company's products.
cards.body:
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky announced plans to establish a dedicated AI research lab for the company. Chesky previously explained that Airbnb had not partnered with existing large language model providers because their current offerings didn't align with the company's needs.

The internal lab will allow Airbnb to develop AI capabilities specifically designed for its travel platform. This move positions Airbnb alongside other major consumer technology companies that are building proprietary AI research teams to create custom tools and features for their services.

cards.headline: Mangrove forests show recovery after decades of decline
cards.teaser: Mangrove forests are experiencing a resurgence following years of damage from human activity.
cards.body:
Mangrove forests are making an unexpected recovery after decades of destruction caused by human activity. This comeback is beneficial for both coastal communities and the climate. The forests provide essential protection against storms and flooding while also sequestering carbon to help address climate change.

The regeneration reflects the resilience of these ecosystems and demonstrates the positive impact of reduced human pressure in certain areas. As mangrove restoration becomes increasingly recognized as important for coastal defense and climate adaptation, these swampy forests are staging a significant environmental turnaround.

hero.headline: Robinson takes five wickets in Test return against New Zealand
hero.body:
England bowler Ollie Robinson completed a five-wicket haul on his return to Test cricket at Lord's against New Zealand. The performance marked a successful comeback for the pace bowler in the ongoing Test match.

Robinson's five-wicket haul demonstrated his effectiveness after time away from the Test arena. The achievement came during play at Lord's Cricket Ground in London, one of cricket's most historic venues. His performance helped England's bowling attack against the touring New Zealand side.

The five-wicket haul is a significant milestone for any bowler in Test cricket, reflecting dominance over a batting lineup in a single innings. Robinson's return to form provides England with a boost to their pace bowling options. Test cricket remains the longest format of the sport, with matches lasting up to five days.

Robinson's successful return adds depth to England's bowling resources as they face New Zealand. The timing of his performance strengthens his case for continued selection in the Test side. Five-wicket hauls are recorded when a bowler dismisses five batsmen in a single innings, a benchmark of individual bowling excellence in cricket.

The match at Lord's continues as part of the Test series between England and New Zealand. Robinson's contribution with the ball gives England a strong position in the contest. His performance will likely influence selection decisions for upcoming Test matches.

cards.headline: St Mirren appoints Craig McLeish as manager on three-year contract
cards.teaser: Craig McLeish has agreed a three-year deal to manage St Mirren, citing his academy background with the club as key to his appointment.
cards.body:
Craig McLeish has been appointed as manager of St Mirren on a three-year contract. McLeish believes his experience with the club's academy provides him with the ideal foundation for the role, giving him insight into the club's youth development system and emerging talent.

The appointment offers St Mirren continuity with a manager who has an established connection to the organization's academy structure.

cards.headline: Graham Potter discusses Sweden World Cup qualification after Chelsea and West Ham exits
cards.teaser: Graham Potter expressed joy and pride in leading Sweden to the World Cup following his dismissals from Chelsea and West Ham.
cards.body:
Graham Potter spoke about his experience taking Sweden to the World Cup after being dismissed from managerial positions at Chelsea and West Ham. Potter described feeling joy and pride in the achievement with the Swedish national team.

The manager's comments addressed the contrast between his club management exits and his success with Sweden. Potter's tenure at both Chelsea and West Ham ended in dismissal before he took the Sweden role.

cards.headline: Audi pushes to keep turbos in Formula One engine regulations
cards.teaser: Audi stated it wants turbo engines to remain part of Formula One when new engine specifications are introduced in 2030 or 2031.
cards.body:
Audi has stated its position that turbocharged engines should remain a feature of Formula One's next generation of power units, scheduled to debut in 2030 or 2031.

The manufacturer's stance contributes to ongoing discussions within the sport about the technical specifications for future engines. As Audi prepares to enter Formula One, its preference for turbo technology plays a role in shaping the direction of these regulatory conversations.

cards.headline: Khadija Shaw and Yui Hasegawa shortlisted for PFA Women's Player of the Year
cards.teaser: Manchester City players Khadija Shaw and Yui Hasegawa are among the nominees for the PFA Women's Player of the Year award.
cards.body:
Manchester City duo Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw and Yui Hasegawa have been shortlisted for the Professional Footballers Association's Women's Player of the Year award.

The PFA award is voted on by fellow professional players, making it one of the most prestigious individual honors in women's football.

cards.headline: FIFA demands payment from fans mistakenly given free World Cup tickets
cards.teaser: FIFA told fans who received free tickets to World Cup group stage matches in Toronto due to an error that they must pay within seven days or forfeit the seats.
cards.body:
FIFA has demanded that fans who mistakenly received complimentary tickets to World Cup group stage matches in Toronto pay for them. The organization gave ticket holders a seven-day deadline to complete payment or forfeit their seats.

FIFA acknowledged responsibility for the ticketing error but still requires affected fans to purchase the tickets they initially obtained at no cost.

cards.headline: Six players nominated for PFA men's player of the year award
cards.teaser: Declan Rice, Gabriel, David Raya, Bruno Fernandes, Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki have been shortlisted for the PFA men's player of the year award.
cards.body:
The Professional Footballers' Association has announced its six nominees for the men's player of the year award. The shortlist features Arsenal players Declan Rice, Gabriel and David Raya, alongside Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United, Manchester City's Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

The award is determined by votes from professional players and recognizes the standout performer in English football. Arsenal's three representatives on the shortlist underscores the club's successful season.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy killed in stabbing at 81
hero.body:
James Handy, a veteran actor known for character roles in Top Gun: Maverick and Jumanji, has died following a stabbing at his Los Angeles home. He was 81 years old.

Police discovered Handy unconscious in the front yard of his Tarzana, California residence at 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday. He had sustained multiple stab wounds to the chest. Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, was arrested at the scene and charged on suspicion of murder. Bail was set at $2 million.

According to the Los Angeles Police Department, the 911 caller stated: "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin." When officers arrived, Gledhill told them he was "the one they were looking for." The police statement noted that the suspect resides at the location with his mother, who is the victim's girlfriend.

Handy built a lengthy career in entertainment that began in 1977 on the television series Ryan's Hope. Over the decades, he appeared in numerous film and television productions, often taking on supporting character roles in major studio projects. Beyond Jumanji and Top Gun: Maverick, his credits included appearances in Logan, K-911, Law and Order, NCIS: Los Angeles, and Criminal Minds. His most recent film work was Top Gun: Maverick in 2022.

Born in New York City, Handy became a familiar presence to audiences through his work across both blockbuster films and smaller productions. Though his name may not be as widely recognized as some of his co-stars, he contributed to many acclaimed projects throughout his four-decade career.

The Los Angeles Police Department continues to investigate the circumstances surrounding Handy's death. Details about what occurred at the actor's home are expected to emerge through court proceedings as the case moves forward in the criminal justice system.

Handy's death marks another loss for the entertainment community during a period that has seen the passing of several notable figures in recent days.

cards.headline: Mobo Awards founder Kanya King dies at 57
cards.teaser: Kanya King, founder of the Mobo Awards, has died from cancer at age 57.
cards.body:
Kanya King, the visionary founder of the Mobo Awards, has died at the age of 57 following cancer. The awards she established became a major platform for celebrating Black music and culture in the UK, recognizing talent across numerous genres.

Following her death, prominent figures from the entertainment industry paid tribute to King's legacy. Stars including Stormzy, Alesha Dixon, and Idris Elba shared memories of her significant contributions to British music and her pivotal role in creating a space to honour Black artists.

cards.headline: Ed Sheeran performs surprise waterfront show
cards.teaser: The singer performed half a dozen songs to hundreds of fans during an early morning waterfront concert.
cards.body:
Ed Sheeran performed an impromptu concert at a waterfront location, drawing hundreds of fans to the early morning show. The singer played approximately six songs during the surprise appearance.

The spontaneous performance gave fans an unexpected opportunity to see Sheeran in an informal setting. Such impromptu concerts have become occasional features of the singer's interaction with audiences, though they are not formally announced in advance.

cards.headline: Scary Movie reboot takes in $7.5 million in previews
cards.teaser: The comedy spoof earned $7.5 million in Thursday night previews, approaching the levels seen by Scream 7.
cards.body:
The new Scary Movie film earned $7.5 million during Thursday night preview screenings, matching performance levels achieved by Scream 7. The strong preview numbers indicate the rebooted comedy franchise still attracts audiences.

The Guardian's review notes that successful jokes are scarce in this sixth installment of the parody series. The film takes aim at multiple horror franchises including Scream, though critics suggest it may not capture the sharp comedic timing that defined earlier entries in the series.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt on set as Isle of Man motorcycle film begins shooting
cards.teaser: Brad Pitt has arrived on set of the Amazon MGM Studios motorcycle racing film as production kicks off on the Isle of Man.
cards.body:
Brad Pitt's production company Plan B is producing "Isle of Man," an Amazon MGM Studios film starring Channing Tatum and Eve Hewson. Filming has begun on the Isle of Man, a small island in the Irish Sea, with cameras rolling as the island's famous motorcycle race takes place.

The timing allows the filmmakers to capture authentic racing atmosphere and footage during the actual event that inspired the film.

cards.headline: Steve Lacy teases third album with new single
cards.teaser: The musician released The Feeling, a new single previewing his upcoming album Oh Yeah?
cards.body:
Steve Lacy has released a new single called "The Feeling," offering a glimpse of his upcoming third studio album, Oh Yeah?, arriving in July. The track delves into themes of longing and heartbreak, continuing Lacy's exploration of personal and romantic emotions.

As both a solo artist and member of the band The Internet, Lacy has cultivated a dedicated following by blending R&B, funk, and alternative music across his work.

cards.headline: Chinese drama Dear You heads to international theaters
cards.teaser: The Teochew-dialect family drama will begin a global theatrical run starting June 18.
cards.body:
Dear You, a family drama filmed in the Teochew dialect, will receive an international theatrical release starting June 18. Damai Entertainment, formerly known as Alibaba Pictures, is handling the worldwide distribution of the film, which has become a significant box office story in China in 2026.

Directed by Lan Hongchun, the film follows Xiaowei, a young grandson navigating family relationships. The drama has resonated with Chinese audiences, and distributors are now testing its appeal in international markets where Chinese-language films have found growing audiences in recent years.

hero.headline: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement funding through 2028
hero.body:
The Senate voted early Friday morning to fund President Trump's immigration enforcement agencies through the end of his second term, allocating $70 billion to Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol operations over the next three years.

The legislation passed on a party-line vote of 52-47 following an 18-hour marathon session known as a "vote-a-rama," during which senators proposed unlimited amendments. Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska was the only member of her party to vote against the bill, while Democratic Senator Michael Bennet of Colorado did not vote.

The passage came after weeks of uncertainty and fierce internal debate over controversial provisions. A central point of contention was a proposed $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund that would allow the administration to issue financial settlements to people connected to the January 6 insurrection. Senate Democrats attempted to strip this provision from the bill through an amendment introduced by Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer. The amendment failed by a single vote, 49-50, with three vulnerable Republican senators breaking ranks to join all Democrats in support.

The debate also involved Republican resistance to initially proposed spending for White House renovations, which Senate leadership ultimately dropped from the bill.

Democratic Senator Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota expressed her frustration with the outcome. "Your tax dollars should not be going to Jan. 6th rioters who went after officers," she wrote on X. "And why give MORE money to ICE when they're already bigger than the FBI?"

Democratic Senator Alex Padilla of California highlighted concerns about immigration enforcement practices, citing deaths of Americans and detention of children, stating that thousands of children have been jailed since the administration began and that ICE has been found to violate the Constitution in more than 10,000 rulings by judges appointed by both Democratic and Republican presidents.

Republican supporters characterized the funding as essential. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Republicans were prioritizing Trump's interests over working families. "The Republican agenda is now written in black and white: A slush fund for Trump, tax dodges for Trump, a ballroom for Trump, and a private militia for Trump. For hard-working Americans? Nothing," Schumer stated.

In contrast, Republican Senator Lindsey Graham expressed satisfaction with the outcome, saying he was "very proud of my Republican colleagues for sticking together and making sure that Border Patrol and ICE are fully funded."

The bill now moves to the House of Representatives for consideration, where it is expected to be taken up next week. The legislation represents a major priority for the Trump administration, securing resources for immigration enforcement operations throughout the remainder of his term.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats block surveillance law extension over intelligence director appointment
cards.teaser: Democrats prevented debate from starting on extending spy powers due to expire next week.
cards.body:
Senate Democrats blocked a procedural motion early Friday to begin debate on extending enhanced surveillance authorities set to expire June 12. All Senate Democrats except John Fetterman of Pennsylvania voted against the motion.

The blockade protests President Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence. The Section 702 foreign surveillance authority, which enables expanded monitoring of foreign targets, faces lapse without congressional action.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official secured the Democratic nomination in New Mexico.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico on Friday. Haaland previously served in the Biden administration.

If elected in the general election, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in United States history. The primary victory positions her as the Democratic nominee heading into the November election.

cards.headline: California governor primary results show Hilton and Becerra leading
cards.teaser: Republicans and Democrats compete for nominations to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Results from California's governor primary show Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra leading their respective party contests. Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra are competing for the Democratic nomination, while Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton vie for their party's spot.

The primary determines who will compete in the general election to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. California's gubernatorial race is among the most closely watched state elections this cycle.

cards.headline: FBI Director says local officials delayed federal help in Nancy Guthrie case
cards.teaser: Kash Patel told NewsNation that accepting FBI assistance is up to local authorities.
cards.body:
FBI Director Kash Patel said local authorities in the Nancy Guthrie case delayed accepting help from federal investigators. Patel made the comments in an interview with NewsNation on Friday.

Patel stated that it is up to local authorities to decide whether they want to accept FBI assistance. The director's comments address the coordination between federal and local law enforcement in the ongoing case.

cards.headline: Medical researchers announce cancer treatment breakthroughs
cards.teaser: Recent advances show results from decades of scientific investment, though treatments extend life rather than cure.
cards.body:
Researchers announced promising breakthroughs against cancers and other deadly diseases in the past month. The advances represent the payoff from decades of scientific investment in medical innovation.

The new treatments share a common limitation: they extend patients' lives by years rather than curing diseases outright. The ongoing medical care required for these treatments represents a significant economic consideration in the current era of medicine.

cards.headline: James Carville offers assessment of Democratic Party challenges
cards.teaser: The Democratic strategist said addressing problems requires honesty about them.
cards.body:
Democratic strategist James Carville provided an assessment of the party's current situation. Carville emphasized that addressing problems requires being honest about them.

Carville's comments come as Democrats conduct internal reviews following recent electoral results. The veteran political consultant has been a prominent voice in Democratic Party strategy for decades.
